title: Cohort-constrained Admission Scheduler and Safety Contracts for Canary Rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's current canary primitives support fixed step schedules and simple percentage splits, but lack fine-grained cohort constraints, probe shadowing, and contract-based auto-rollback. This ticket designs and implements a Cohort-Constrained Admission Scheduler (CCAS) that: enforces per-cohort traffic budgets, applies safety contracts (metric guards, quorum thresholds, and entropy budgets), supports shadow/probe traffic with configurable sampling, and exposes a compact DSL for declarative rollout policies.

Goals:
- Allow rollouts to target named cohorts (e.g., internal-beta, 1% sampled new users, paid-tier) with independent step calendars and guardrails.
- Implement safety contracts: metric-based thresholds (latency p95, error-rate), quorum rules (minimum sample counts across cohorts), and entropy limits to prevent rapid oscillations.
- Support shadow probing with differential sampling rates and optional golden-path comparison.
- Provide automatic rollback triggers with hysteresis and step-back strategies (instant rollback, step-back-by-n, or slow-down-to-minimum).
- Expose a declarative policy DSL that maps to runtime enforcement and to Console UX.

High-level design summary:
- Admission Scheduler core enforces policy by slicing incoming traffic according to cohort selectors and active step definitions. Cohort selectors can be based on request attributes (account tier, region, session id hashing).
- Safety Contracts runtime subscribes to telemetry (token-level latency, per-request error tags, model output regressions) and evaluates contract predicates at each step boundary and continuously for rolling checks.
- Rollout Controller implements state machine: PREPARING -> PROBING (shadow) -> GRADUAL -> STABLE. Transitions require contract passes and quorum. Failure modes trigger configured mitigation: "immediate-rollback", "step-back-n", or "throttle-to-min".
- A lightweight quota engine enforces per-cohort traffic budgets and burst allowances.

Config DSL example (intent is compact but expressive):

policy: "cohort_constrained_canary_v1"
cohorts:
  - name: internal-beta
    selector: "user.segment == 'internal'"
    schedule:
      - step: 0
        pct: 5
        duration: 2m
      - step: 1
        pct: 20
        duration: 1h
  - name: sampled-new-users
    selector: "hash(user.id) % 1000 < 10"
    schedule:
      - step: 0
        pct: 0.5
        duration: 10m
      - step: 1
        pct: 2
        duration: 2h
safety_contracts:
  - id: latency-p95-bound
    metric: "latency.p95_ms"
    op: "<="
    value: 400
    window: 5m
  - id: error-rate-threshold
    metric: "errors.per_1000_requests"
    op: "<="
    value: 5
    window: 5m
  - id: regression-diff
    metric: "semantic-regression.score_drop_pct"
    op: "<="
    value: 2
    window: 15m
quorum:
  min_samples_per_cohort: 100
  min_total_samples: 1000
rollback_policy:
  on_violation: "step-back-1"
  max_step_backs: 3
  cool_down: 30m
probe_traffic:
  enabled: true
  shadow_sample_pct: 1
  golden_compare: true

Telemetry and signals:
- Primary signals: latency.p50/p95/p99, errors.per_1000_requests, semantic-regression.* (embedding similarity or eval score deltas), request volume per cohort.
- We will store rollup series at 10s resolution for short windows and 1m for longer retention.
- Alerts: contract violation, quorum shortfall, sustained oscillation (>3 step-backs in hour).

API & Console integration:
- API: PATCH /rollouts/{id}/policy accepts DSL payload; GET /rollouts/{id}/state exposes per-cohort step, observed metrics, and contract evaluation results.
- Console: rollout timeline (per-cohort lanes), live guardrail indicators, suggested mitigations (auto-suggested slow-downs and probe increases). UX should allow one-click promote/rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit+integration tests for scheduler deterministic routing logic and contract evaluation.
- End-to-end canary demo: deploy model variant A -> B with two cohorts (internal-beta and sampled-new-users) and show automated step promotions and a simulated contract violation causing configured mitigation.
- API documentation, Console mockups, and a migration guide for existing rollout configs.

Risks & constraints:
- Telemetry lag may cause false positives; mitigation: require minimum sample counts and hysteresis windows before triggering punitive actions.
- Complex selectors could increase runtime cost; limit selector language to simple expressions initially.
- Security: ensure DSL doesn't allow exfiltration of PII in logs; security review required.

2026-02-25 Hannah Lee: Design review — Console lanes proposed. Need per-cohort error drilldown and a compact summary card that surfaces which contract failed. Attached mock: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/ccas/overview.png
2026-03-01 Rahul Desai: Telemetry plan reviewed with Observability. Recommend 10s rollups for p95 and error counters; will add a light-weight contract-eval service to subscribe to metric streams.

2026-03-05 Ravi Patel: Integration tests added for rollback_policy=step-back-1 and max_step_backs=3. Simulated fault (injected latency) produces expected step-back behavior in 2/3 runs; investigating non-determinism in low-sample windows.
2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Security sign-off pending on DSL parsing sandboxing. Raised sec ticket SEC-2108 as dependency.

notes: This ticket intentionally favors conservative defaults (small initial cohorts, strict quorum) to minimize blast radius. The DSL supports future extensions (rate-limited canary, ML-driven step sizing).
